newsitem.title: USA: FGIC quits short-term money management business.
newsitem.headline: FGIC quits short-term money management business.

text.p: Financial Guaranty Insurance Co said it has stopped managing investments for local governments and transferred assets from the venture to General Electric Co's GE Investment Management Inc.

"We decided that the short-term money management business didn't fit our strategic aims of the company," a FGIC spokeswoman, Lisa Kunze, said in a telephone interview. FGIC is a unit of GE's GE Capital Services.
FGIC managed a total of $300 million from two short-term funds it ran through its FGIC Public Trust operation. Both funds remain SEC-registered following the transfer, Kunze said.

With the move, the FGIC Public Trust U.S. Treasury Money Market Fund was renamed Financial Investors Trust U.S. Treasury Money Market Fund. The FGIC Public Trust U.S. Government Money Market Fund was renamed Financial Investors Trust U.S. Government Money Market Fund.
Standard & Poor's Corp said it affirmed both funds at its highest rating, AAAm, after the transfers, reflecting the funds' "superior capacity to maintain principal and limit exposure to loss."
Investors in the funds are primarily municipal entities including towns, counties and state agencies. ALPS Mutual Fund Services will continue as the funds' administrator, FGIC said.
James McCullough, formerly the chief investment officer of FGIC Advisors, left the company, Kunze said, adding that he was the only FGIC executive affected by the fund transfer.
